Swap at 97% and load 14–18 with nothing building are the largest slowdowns measured on the Mac (parallel-proof § Measured baseline): every budget there reads INCONCLUSIVE by load. Clean up first; no code changes.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Hygiene](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#9-hygiene-do-first-no-design-needed)

### Scope
- Prune worktrees whose branches are merged (47 on the Mac today) down to those with open PRs; same policy on the Spark
- Delete `target/` in worktrees idle more than three days. Worktrees on open branches with large targets (`off-case-guards`, `issue-824`, `issue-45`, `issue-39` at last count) are listed for the owner, never deleted by an agent
- Remove orphaned proof-run copies under the temp directory whose creating process is gone (checked by PID, never by name)
- At most three resident sessions on the Mac, one of them proving
- Free disk before and after is a reading (bays later need about 40 GB, parallel-proof § Hygiene)
- Readings only: no script, no option, no config key is added

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On the Mac, idle (no cargo, vitest or proof running), `sysctl vm.swapusage` shows under 50% of swap used and the 1-minute load is under 8, both read three times five minutes apart and saved (moved to #2673)
- [ ] No worktree on an open branch and no uncommitted edit was removed: the before and after lists of worktrees, with `git status --porcelain` per remaining worktree, are saved

### Proof
The saved command outputs before and after, on both machines.

### Depends on
- none

Budgets refuse to count at load above the core count (invariant 2), so two sessions proving at once turn each other's budgets INCONCLUSIVE. Add `scripts/throttle.mjs`: a host-local, flock-based lock table under `~/.deepbuild/throttle/` with four classes, and route `lanes.mjs` commands through it.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Scheduling](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#6-scheduling-a-per-machine-throttle-table) · related #1015 (the product's lease for users' repos; this is the repo's own tooling and never imports it)

### Scope
- Classes and limits: **build** (Mac 1, Spark 2, top-level outside proofs: cargo build, `cargo test`, `npm run build`, clippy; the default for an unlisted command), **bay pair** (Mac 1, Spark 3; a counting semaphore whose grant index k names `~/deepbuild-bays/<k>/`; tested here with a stub holder, T1 is its only real caller), **test** (Mac 2, Spark 4: vitest parallel block, `node --test`), **timed** (1, exclusive of all classes, waits for load < cores)
- `throttle.mjs <class> [--wait <min>] -- <command>` acquires, runs, releases and exits with the child's status (128 + signal when killed). An importable `acquire(class)`/`release(grant)` entry serves `proof-runs.mjs`, `preflight.mjs` and `perf.mjs`
- Inherited grants: a held grant is exported as `DEEP_THROTTLE=<class>:<id>`; descendants pass through for `build` and `test`. `timed` never passes through unless an ancestor holds `timed`. `DEEP_THROTTLE` is verified (lock table, live holder pid, holder in the requester's parent-pid chain), never trusted
- Drain: a `timed` request stops new top-level grants and waits for every holder outside its own chain to finish or to have a descendant blocked in a throttle wait. A bay-pair holder never counts as idle for a top-level `timed`; it does for a nested one. Nested requests from current holders go before new top-level ones
- Grant waits per caller (section 6 table): lane command 30 min, `timed` inside a `proof-runs.mjs` spawn 15 min, a measured run's top-level `timed` 60 min, `affected.mjs` jobs 30 min. On timeout: first line `INCONCLUSIVE no grant`, non-zero exit
- `preflight.mjs` and `perf.mjs` claim `timed` before their timers start and hold it to the end; perf's lock is taken only under `timed` and accepts a lock held by an ancestor (`DEEP_PERF_LOCK=<pid>`, verified like `DEEP_THROTTLE`)
- Once #1015's `deep lease` runs in this repo, a `timed` drain must also wait on `deep lease` holders on the machine; until then #1015 leaves commands under this script alone, so the two never meet
- `lanes.mjs` wraps its commands by the section 6 classification (one additive edit). `throttle.mjs` and `perf.mjs` join the guard regex, so this PR carries a signed approval tag

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A wrapped command that exits 3 makes `throttle.mjs` exit 3, and one killed by SIGTERM exits 143
- [ ] A no-grant timeout exits non-zero with `INCONCLUSIVE no grant` as its first line
- [ ] A nested `timed` request under a `build` holder still drains: no other grant starts until it ends; nested `build` and `test` pass through
- [ ] The throttle log shows no top-level `timed` grant started at load > cores (a nested `timed` under a preflight or perf grant passes through by design)
- [ ] A forged `DEEP_THROTTLE` is ignored and a fresh grant is requested
- [ ] Two `timed` requests nested in different chains both complete in request order without hitting the timeout; so do two chains that each hold a bay pair and each make a nested `timed` request
- [ ] A preflight, and separately a perf run started by hand, that requests `timed` while another session holds the Mac's bay pair waits until the pair is released, then completes, and preflight's perf child is not BLOCKED
- [ ] Each caller's grant wait matches the section 6 table
- [ ] A preflight run's measured time contains no throttle wait: the grant precedes the timer
- [ ] After a 14-minute `timed` wait, the before lane's timed set still gets its full 20-minute `TIMEOUT`
- [ ] `throttle.mjs` and `perf.mjs` are in the guard regex: an unsigned change to either fails the guard

### Proof
Tooling tests on real processes with stub holders; each planted wrong program (a wrapper that exits 0, a `timed` that passes through, a trusted `DEEP_THROTTLE`) shown failing first.

### Depends on
- #1111 TD (docs/parallel-proof.md)
- #1112 T0 (load and swap low enough to measure grant waits)

`affected.mjs` and the before and trace lanes run budget tests beside whatever the machine is doing, so they read INCONCLUSIVE by load or, worse, count a neighbour's load against the change. Name the timed tests once and run them only under a `timed` grant.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Rollout, T9](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#12-rollout-and-proof-of-each-step) · split from design step T9 to stay under 400 lines; T9b holds the skip rules

### Scope
- `lanes.mjs` exports an explicit `timed` list, guarded like `alone`. Seed: the test files that call `environmentProblem(` at their own call site, plus files calling `judgeTiming`, `judgeLimit`, `referenceMacProblem` or `notReference` (e.g. `881/latency`, `857/speedup`, `854/idle`, `896/settled`, `140/view/timing`), plus files that gate on a helper's `status === 'INCONCLUSIVE'` (e.g. `tests/acceptance/365/budgets.test.ts:47`). An import-closure rule was tried and marks 386 files, so it is not used. Every summary prints the list it used
- `affected.mjs` skips timed files unless `--timed`; with `--timed` it runs them through `throttle.mjs timed`. Its own commands go through the throttle: workspace build, clippy and `cargo test -p` as `build`; the vitest block and `node --test` as `test`
- `proof-runs.mjs` splits the before and trace lanes' tagged files into a timed and an untimed set (one serial spawn today, `:293`), acquires a `timed` grant through `throttle.mjs`'s `acquire()` (waiting up to 15 minutes) and only then spawns the timed set, so the 20-minute per-spawn `TIMEOUT` (`:245`) covers the run, not the wait. Additive and guarded
- `affected.mjs` joins the guard regex. `lanes.mjs` and `proof-runs.mjs` are guarded today, so the PR carries a signed approval tag

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With no flag, timed files in the affected set are not run and the summary is INCONCLUSIVE, listing them; with no timed file in the affected set, PASS remains possible
- [ ] With `--timed`, the throttle log shows the timed grant around the timed files
- [ ] Every file calling `environmentProblem(`, `judgeTiming`, `judgeLimit`, `referenceMacProblem` or `notReference` is in the `timed` list, checked by a test that greps the tree; a planted list missing one fails, naming the file
- [ ] In the before and trace lanes the timed set's spawn starts only after its grant, and a 14-minute grant wait leaves its full 20-minute `TIMEOUT`
- [ ] Failures on main equal today's: a run on main before and after the change lists the same FAIL ids

### Proof
Tooling tests on fixture trees with real `throttle.mjs`; the grep test; before/after failure lists on main.

### Depends on
- #1113 T5 (throttle)

An existing invariant-2 hole: `affected.mjs` drops skips (their type is neither pass nor fail, `:281-282`) and summarises PASS when nothing failed (`:424`), and `lanes.mjs:262-268` reads a test that asserts `'INCONCLUSIVE: …'` (`requireGpu()`, `tests/acceptance/380/helpers.ts:153`, about 25 files) as FAIL. Under invariant 2 a skip is unrun, never PASS.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Rollout, T9](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#12-rollout-and-proof-of-each-step) · [Open owner decision](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#10a-open-owner-decision-gates-t9)

> **DECISION FOR OWNER (gates this issue; asked once, section 10a).**
> 1. `380/cts-exact.test.ts:288` skips `BLOCKED: no record from an M1 …` unless `DEEPBUILD_M1_RECORD` is set. **(a, recommended)** a `skips` entry may list an approved BLOCKED-by-design test; the lane keeps the state its other tests give and every summary prints the listed BLOCKED test. **(b)** the lane stays BLOCKED until the record exists.
> 2. About 218 skip sites, many `ctx.skip('INCONCLUSIVE (reading only)…')`. **(a, recommended)** a reading-only skip is listable, keyed on test id and the full note; never for a file in the `timed` list or a test carrying a criterion tag. **(b)** each makes its lane INCONCLUSIVE when it fires.
> Before this lands, a run of the unit lane on main lists every pass the new rule turns INCONCLUSIVE, with its skip site; that list goes to the owner with these two questions.

### Scope
- **Test states.** In `lanes.mjs`, as `stateOf` already does in `affected.mjs` (`:267`), a test whose failure message starts with INCONCLUSIVE or BLOCKED takes that state
- **Skips.** A skip makes the summary INCONCLUSIVE and is listed, unless its test id **and** exact note prefix are in a new `skips` list in `scripts/known-failures.json` with a reason and the approval that retired or gated it. A skip whose note starts with BLOCKED makes the lane BLOCKED. The list holds only retired tests and tests gated on an opt-in environment variable (plus the classes the owner allows above). Platform and GPU skips are never listed and leave the lane INCONCLUSIVE (platform). A listed skip is printed in every summary and does not change the lane's state. Known today: `327/answers.test.ts:28` (retired AC2), `packages/pi/test/lifecycle.test.ts:37` (`DEEP_PI_CLI`), `880/touch-id.test.ts:45` and `880/redraft/touch-id.test.ts:296` (`DEEP_880_TOUCH_ID`); `684/lean.test.ts:42` keeps BLOCKED and is not listed. The PR enumerates the list with a scan on main
- **Signed key.** A new key-level rule in `proof-guard.mjs`: any change to the `skips` key needs a signed approval tag. Scoped to that key, because `affected.mjs --record` rewrites the rest of the file on main. The approver, not a parser, confirms a gate is an opt-in variable or a retirement
- **Reporters.** `scripts/proof-vitest-reporter.mjs:14` keeps each skip and its note (`TestResult.note`); `lanes.mjs` vitest commands (`:68-69`) switch to it; `node --test` (`:73`) switches to a reporter that records `t.skip` and `{ skip }` per test
- **No grant.** When `throttle.mjs` ends a vitest job with no grant it leaves a marker; those files read INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL "reported no test" (`affected.mjs:397-405`)
- **Evidence record.** Each lane writes a record: host, platform, tree hash, per-test states. T7 and T8 consume it
- Guarded files throughout, so a signed approval tag

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `lanes.mjs` unit run with an unlisted skip reports the lane INCONCLUSIVE and lists the skip; one whose note starts with BLOCKED reports BLOCKED
- [ ] A test failing with `INCONCLUSIVE: …` reads INCONCLUSIVE in `lanes.mjs`, not FAIL
- [ ] A listed id skipping under a different note than its entry's makes the lane INCONCLUSIVE; with `DEEP_880_TOUCH_ID` set on a machine that is not the reference Mac, 880's listed opt-in entry does not cover its `notReference()` skip and the lane is INCONCLUSIVE
- [ ] With `--timed`, a run in which any budget skips INCONCLUSIVE summarises INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS
- [ ] A change to the `skips` key without a signed approval tag fails the guard; an `affected.mjs --record` rewrite of the other keys passes it
- [ ] A vitest job ended with no grant reads INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL
- [ ] Each lane's evidence record names host, platform, tree hash and every test's state
- [ ] Failures on main equal today's

### Proof
Tooling tests with fixture suites that skip under each note kind; the guard on a signed and an unsigned `skips` edit; the before-landing list of passes turned INCONCLUSIVE, sent to the owner.

### Depends on
- #1114 T9a (timed list and throttle routing)
- the owner's two decisions above

Agents run day and night, so no idle period exists for budgets, and a per-PR budget queue was the efficiency bottleneck (owner decision, 2026-11-02). Budgets leave the PR's path but stay tied to each commit: PRs with reference-Mac budget criteria merge as `Part of #n` on their other criteria, and a budget window measures them later.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Budget windows](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#12a-budget-windows-owner-decision-2026-11-02)

### Scope
- A few times a day `throttle.mjs` opens a budget window on each reference Mac: it stops granting `build`, `test` and `bay pair`, lets running grants finish, runs `scripts/budget-window.mjs`, then reopens. Agents keep thinking and editing; only their next build or test waits
- `budget-window.mjs` measures every commit merged since the last window, each against its own merge base, 20 samples a side as `docs/technical-design.md` sets, with budget numbers unchanged
- One evidence record per commit (the T9b record shape). A pass closes that commit's issue when its other criteria are already proven; a miss leaves the issue open naming the regression and the commit, and files a budget follow-up; a commit not yet measured leaves its issue open, never closed
- Agents never run or edit the window: `budget-window.mjs` joins the guard regex (signed approval tag)

Runs on: Mac only (reference Mac)

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A window drains every slot before its first sample and reopens after its last
- [ ] Three commits merged between windows get three records, each against its own merge base
- [ ] A planted 2× regression in one of them leaves only that issue open, naming that commit
- [ ] A commit merged during a window is measured in the next one
- [ ] An agent's build requested during a window starts within a minute of the window ending

### Proof
A fixture repository with three merged commits and a planted regression, run through a real window on the reference Mac; the throttle log around the window.

### Overlaps (consolidation, Nov 6)
- Budget criteria waiting for this: #1009 (AC12 of #30) and #1303 (AC6 of #1018)

### Depends on
- #1111 TD (the technical-design line), #1113 T5 (throttle), #1114 T9a and #1115 T9b (timed list, skip states and the evidence record)
- #1404 perf counts only the parent process's instructions, so a slower child can read PASS

Every proof-lane copy starts with a cold `target/` (`preflight.mjs:11` deletes `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; git-archive copies start without one), and a target moved to a new path keeps the old path baked in through `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` (21 files in 10 crates), which would run the base's binaries against the change's tests. Add `scripts/bays.mjs`: fixed-path workspaces `~/deepbuild-bays/<k>/` in pairs, each replaced in place to the run's exact tree and built incrementally.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Build reuse](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#4-build-reuse-fixed-path-workspaces-not-relocated-targets)

### Scope
- Pairs: Mac 1, Spark 3, claimed through T5's `bay pair` class (`bays.mjs` is its only caller). Only a proof rooted in a worktree of the machine's repository with no ancestor holding a pair gets one; `tests/proof.test.mjs`, the 569 scene proofs and other test-started proofs keep temporary copies
- Replace in place: write only files whose bytes differ from disk (full `listFiles` contents: git archive of the tree hash, uncommitted bundle, untracked non-ignored files; all three hashes recorded), delete files absent from the tree, never backdate an mtime. `.git` recreated each run with `alternates` to the root's common dir. Kept across runs: `target/` and `node_modules/` only. `packages/*/dist` deleted before the workspace build
- `undoBuild` in a bay skips `.git`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, and its copy-back skips files whose bytes match
- `bays.mjs` removes `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` from the environment it hands bay builds and tests (not in `childEnv`)
- Seal: at release, a stat listing (path, size, mtime_ns, inode) of all of `target/` and `node_modules/` plus the tree hash; at claim, any mismatch deletes both and builds cold, recorded. `npm ci` is keyed on lock bytes and a post-install marker. Stated plainly: bays are weaker than today's proof lane and equal to today's perf; the record binds sources, not the target
- Lock holder death releases the bay. Rollback is reverting the PR; no fallback flag. `bays.mjs` is in the guard regex from this PR (signed approval tag). This PR adds the bay owner only; T2 moves proof copies into bays
- Spark criteria exclude deep-app and its five dependents until T8

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A second run of the same tree in a bay compiles 0 crates
- [ ] A run after an aborted run rebuilds every file the abort left different
- [ ] A planted mutant or a rewritten `kit-ledger.json` from a previous run never survives into the next
- [ ] A tampered `target/` (a planted binary and a replaced rlib, not only an edited fingerprint) is detected at claim and built cold, and the record says so
- [ ] Lock holder death releases the bay
- [ ] `tests/proof.test.mjs` and the 569 scene proofs run on temporary copies and take no pair, inside and outside a held pair
- [ ] A bay build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set in the parent environment still writes to `<bay>/target`
- [ ] Bay-target size is a reading

### Proof
Tooling tests on real bays in a scratch home directory; each planted wrong program (blob-id comparison instead of bytes, a relocated target, a trusted seal) shown failing first.

### Depends on
- #1113 T5 (the `bay pair` class)
- #1112 T0 (disk for one pair on the Mac)

The proof lane makes a cold copy per use (base, change, each twin, crash, replay) and runs `npm ci` plus a 26-package build in each (`proof-runs.mjs:140,192`, `proof-suites.mjs:61,111`). Move those copies into T1's bay pair.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Build reuse](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#4-build-reuse-fixed-path-workspaces-not-relocated-targets)

### Scope
- The pair replaces `baseCheckout` and `changeCopy`: the base bay holds the merge base plus the before lane's overlaid test paths (`proof-runs.mjs:369`); the change bay holds the change and, in turn, each twin; crash and replay reuse the pair in the same roles. A bay never flips between base and change
- Before every use (each lane, twin and copy kind) the bay is byte-compare replaced to that use's exact recipe, and the recipe is written into the record per use
- This replaces #569's "runs on the merge base in a temporary checkout" for the base copy: the base now runs in a persistent bay, which is weaker than a temporary checkout and equal to today's perf kept copies (parallel-proof § Build reuse, trust boundary); the record names the bay's seal check
- `npm ci` only when the lock bytes changed; Stryker's `node_modules` relink walk (`:166-176`) is skipped in a bay (`runs.bay`)
- Additive branch in guarded files: signed approval tag

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `npm ci` per proof run is 0 without a lock change and 1 when the change edits the lock, plus 1 in the base bay only when the merge base moved past a lock change
- [ ] Crash's overlay files and the before lane's base overlays are absent from the bays when replay runs, and each use's recipe is in the record
- [ ] A second proof of the same tree, with `origin/main` pinned and an input whose twins, crash overlay and before-lane base overlay touch no Rust, compiles 0 crates in both bays; when they touch Rust, only the crates they touch rebuild, named in the record
- [ ] An untracked tagged test in the worktree is present in the change bay and named in the record
- [ ] Proof wall time before and after on the same commit is a reading

### Proof
Two proof runs of one fixed input on each machine with the cargo and npm logs; a planted copy that keeps the previous use's overlay shown failing first.

### Depends on
- #1117 T1 (bays)

perf keys its kept copies by worktree path (`sha256(realpathSync(root))`, `perf.mjs:28`), so every new session worktree starts both sides cold. Key them per machine (`deepbuild-perf/<machine>/{base,without-tests}`), widen perf's per-checkout lock (`perf.mjs:24-84`) to machine-wide, and replace their trees with the bay byte-compare rule.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Cost cuts](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#5-proof-run-cost-cuts-inside-one-run)

### Scope
- Rekey and lock as above; the lock is still taken only under `timed` (T5)
- Tree replacement uses T1's byte-compare rule; no backdating
- `perf.mjs` is in the guard after T5: signed approval tag

Runs on: Mac only (perf runs only on the Mac)

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A perf run from a second worktree on the same machine compiles 0 crates on its base side, counting perf's own `checks.mjs` builds in the kept copy and not the temporary copies of its nested proof lanes (which build cold by design)
- [ ] The one exception: deep-show and its dependents rebuild when the canvas-kit lane rewrote `kit-ledger.json` with different bytes, and the record names it
- [ ] perf wall time before and after is a reading

### Proof
Two perf runs from two worktrees of one commit, with cargo's compile lines; a planted path-keyed copy shown failing first.

### Depends on
- #1113 T5 (throttle and the guard on `perf.mjs`), #1117 T1 (byte-compare replacement)

Stryker rebuilds every workspace package per mutant. Per mutant, build the mutated package and its dependents from the reverse workspace graph (`tsc -b packages/

` alone builds p and its dependencies, while tests read dependents' dist); `undoBuild` in `proof-runs.mjs` still restores every touched source file. **Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Cost cuts](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#5-proof-run-cost-cuts-inside-one-run) ### Scope - Additive branch in `proof-runs.mjs` (guarded: signed approval tag); no new option - Fixed measurement input: PR #881's head `713bc483` against its merge base `f41a5b3e` (`Closes #881`, tagged tests and twins under `tests/acceptance/881/`, changes `packages/extension-host/src/{host,trust}.ts`, two packages depend on `extension-host`). The measurement worktree sets `refs/remotes/origin/main` to `f41a5b3e` and deletes the timing-gated `latency.test.ts` in a commit of its own; `availableParallelism()` pinned to 2 by an environment-level CPU limit, named in the record Runs on: Spark + Mac ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] On the fixed input, every Stryker run of the lane (one per unproven test plus a grouped run) finishes under its own 80-minute cap (`4 * TIMEOUT`, the Stryker run's timeout in `proof-runs.mjs`) - [ ] The killed and survived sets equal those of one unscoped reference run made with only that Stryker cap lifted, both using only 881's untimed tagged tests, below the load gate - [ ] Mutants that hit the 60 s per-mutant timeout in either run are listed and excluded from the comparison ### Proof The two Stryker reports on the fixed input and their diff; a planted scope that builds only the mutated package (no dependents) shown changing the kill set first. ### Depends on - #1118 T2 (the bay branch that skips the `node_modules` relink)

On the Spark 21 of 27 crates build. deep-app and its five dependents (deep-gpu-layer, deep-panel-host, deep-replica, deep-marks-render, deep-text-render) fail because `image` sits in deep-app's macOS-only dependencies while `picture()` in `crates/deep-app/src/show.rs` uses it unguarded. Fix the Linux breakages #70 needs anyway, and make the Mac's `cargo test` write the reference test list a Spark run is compared against.

Checked on main at 35503ab6: `image` now sits in deep-app's shared dependencies, so the crate count needs a fresh Spark run. At a9d2e682 lsof is chosen per platform in `packages/hub/src/stacks.ts`, `packages/supervisor/src/procs.ts` and `packages/env-local/src/stack.ts`, `O_NOFOLLOW` has its arm64 value in deep-hook, and the spool test makes its folder 0700. Still open: the Mac's reference test list (PR #1694) and every Spark run.

**Epic:** #1 · Part of #70 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Placement](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#3-placement-what-runs-where)

### Scope
- deep-app: `image` usable on Linux, or `picture()` gated to match its dependency
- `/usr/sbin/lsof` hardcoded in `packages/env-local/src/index.ts` and `packages/hub/src/core.ts` (Linux has `/usr/bin/lsof`): resolve from PATH or per platform
- deep-hook: the `O_NOFOLLOW` constant (`crates/deep-hook/src/main.rs:956`) is the x86_64 value, so on aarch64 the symlink refusal does nothing; use the platform's constant
- deep-hook test `a_line_written_to_a_spool_moved_aside…` makes its folder under the umask (0775 on the Spark) and the product correctly refuses a group-writable spool; the test creates it 0700. This edits a test, so it goes as its own approved proposal if the test carries a criterion tag
- The Mac `cargo test` writes `cargo test -- --list` per target into its evidence record (T9b's record)
- Unblocks the Mac-only status of #184, #555 and #851's core slices

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 27 of 27 crates build on the Spark
- [ ] `cargo test` on the Spark has no FAIL or BLOCKED
- [ ] Its record lists the tests absent by platform (four whole test files plus cfg-gated single tests), by comparison with the Mac's reference list, and the lane is INCONCLUSIVE (platform), not PASS
- [ ] A symlinked spool path is refused by deep-hook on aarch64, and the planted x86_64 constant lets it through and fails, naming the path
- [ ] env-resources finds a free port on Linux, and a planted hardcoded `/usr/sbin/lsof` fails there, naming the path

### Proof
Build and test logs from the Spark and the Mac on one commit; the two evidence records; each planted wrong program shown failing on the Spark first.

### Depends on
- #1115 T9b (evidence record and platform skips never PASS)

The Spark has 20 cores and 121 GB but runs nothing for a Mac session today. Add `scripts/lane-remote.mjs --host spark-ts <lane>`: ship the exact tree (commit, uncommitted bundle, untracked non-ignored files) and the merge base computed on the Mac, run the lane in a Spark worktree and bay pair under the Spark's throttle, and fetch the evidence record back.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: Remote lanes](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#8-remote-lanes)

### Scope
- Ship: `git push` of the commit, a bundle of uncommitted changes, a tarball of untracked non-ignored files. The Spark sets its worktree's `refs/remotes/origin/main` to the shipped merge base and refuses the run if the merge base it computes differs; the record names it
- One Spark worktree per session (`~/deepbuild/.claude/worktrees/<name>`), not relocated during its life; proof lanes run from there into a Spark bay pair
- The record names host, platform, tree hash, bundle hash and, for composite trees, their recipe
- Per-test merge: a PR's unit verdict is a Spark run merged with a Mac `--only` run of the ids the Spark skipped plus those reaching a platform-branching source (tests reaching sources that read `process.platform === …`, crates with `cfg(target_os)`, platform-branching helpers). Any FAIL wins. A Spark lint record is a reading, never the lint verdict

Runs on: Spark + Mac

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A PR's merged unit verdict equals a full Mac run on the same tree
- [ ] A planted bug in the darwin-only branch of `packages/record/src/storage.ts`, and one in deep-hook's macOS `args_of`, each make the merged verdict FAIL
- [ ] A Spark FAIL plus a Mac pass of the same test id merges to FAIL
- [ ] A Spark lint record never counts as the lint verdict
- [ ] An untracked tagged test in the session worktree runs on the Spark
- [ ] A shipped merge base that differs from the one the Spark computes refuses the run, naming both

### Proof
One PR's lanes run both ways (merged and full Mac) with both records; each planted wrong program shown failing first.

### Depends on
- #1121 T8 (the Spark builds what it runs), #1115 T9b (evidence record), #1117 T1 and #1118 T2 (Spark bay pairs)

The unit lane's alone block runs 125 entries one at a time (557 s recorded). Up to 29 of its 85 folders are there only because a sibling's cargo build rewrites `target/debug/<bin>`. Build test binaries once per run into a run-private `bin/` (`DEEP_BIN_DIR`) and move those folders to the parallel block.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Parallel proof: The alone block](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#7-the-alone-block-split-by-reason) · [Cost cuts, binaries for tests](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/parallel-proof.md#5-proof-run-cost-cuts-inside-one-run)

### Scope
- `DEEP_BIN_DIR`: the before lane sets it per side from each bay's own build; `childEnv` drops an inherited value **before** merging its `extra` argument (today it merges then deletes, `proof-runs.mjs:44-50`); `lanes.mjs` and `affected.mjs` always set it from their own build, never from the shell
- Move only folders whose sole reason for `alone` is the binary rewrite; the 56 with load or timing gates stay timed; #236's shared sandbox log stream stays alone
- **Gate:** roughly 70–80 acceptance files spawn `cargo` themselves; each needs a blind redraft (AGENTS.md Proof) before it can read `DEEP_BIN_DIR`. Those are separate small blind jobs; this issue lands the mechanism and moves only folders whose files need no redraft or whose redraft has merged. **Owner-approved packaging update (2026-11-12):** use one PR, #2321. Independently drafted redrafts may land as separately reviewable adoption commits before the scheduling commit within that PR. #2336/#2337 are superseded; the approval guard and every moved file's wrong-program-before-removal proof remain required.

Runs on: Mac (required); Spark optional. Owner-approved scope update (2026-11-12): Spark verification is not a closure prerequisite for this issue. Optional Linux/Spark readings must retain their actual platform and status; the four acceptance criteria and Mac proof remain unchanged.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A tagged test that spawns a binary fails on the base side of the before lane when the base's binary is the wrong program: base and change never share binaries
- [ ] An inherited `DEEP_BIN_DIR` in the shell is ignored by `lanes.mjs` and `affected.mjs`, and a per-side value passed to `childEnv` survives

### Proof
Unit-lane runs before and after on one commit; each moved file's planted wrong program failing in the parallel block; a planted `childEnv` that deletes after merging shown failing first.
